prompt: A customer starts shouting about a billing error. Your first instinct is to…

options.text: Find exactly what went wrong in the account before saying much.
Reassure them that I'm here and I'll look after them.
Tell them what I'm going to do right now to fix it.
Keep it human: "Ugh, that's the worst. Let's sort it out."

prompt: Your teammates would most likely describe you as…

options.text: The one who knows the system inside out.
Calm and fair. I can talk to anyone.
Resourceful. I find a way when there isn't one.
Warm. People come to me when they're having a rough day.

prompt: A policy blocks what the customer is asking for. You…

options.text: Explain the policy clearly and why it exists.
Look for a creative workaround within the rules.
Offer the best alternative and move forward quickly.
Acknowledge how disappointing that is before offering options.

prompt: The most satisfying part of a call for you is…

options.text: Cracking a tricky problem nobody else could.
Hearing the relief in the customer's voice.
Closing it fast and clean, with nothing left open.
A good laugh and a genuine connection.

prompt: Which kind of call drains you the most?

options.text: Long emotional calls with no clear problem to solve.
Hostile customers who make it personal.
Rigid, by-the-book calls with no room to improvise.
Switching moods constantly from one call to the next.

prompt: A customer is telling a long story that has little to do with the issue. You…

options.text: Enjoy it and chat along. Rapport matters.
Listen politely, then gently steer back.
Redirect at the first natural pause.
Use something from the story to find a new angle on the fix.

prompt: When you explain something complicated, you tend to…

options.text: Walk through it step by step with the exact details.
Use an everyday analogy they can relate to.
Give the short version and the one action they need to take.
Check in on how they're feeling about it as I go.

prompt: Under pressure (long queue, back-to-back tough calls), you tend to…

options.text: Get more precise and procedural.
Speed up and get more direct.
Apologize more and try to keep everyone happy.
Stay even-keeled on the call, but feel it afterwards.

prompt: A customer asks about something you've never seen before. You…

options.text: Research it thoroughly before giving an answer.
Try a few ideas. Something will work.
Say, "Good question, let's figure it out together."
Stay calm, reassure them, and bring in the right person.

prompt: The feedback you hear most often from supervisors is…

options.text: "Great accuracy. Could show a bit more warmth."
"Customers love you. Watch your handle time."
"Very efficient. Slow down with upset callers."
"Creative solutions. Stick closer to process."
"You handle anyone. Make sure you take your breaks."
